summary: AgentModernize is a 4-agent LangGraph pipeline (legacy analyzer, specification generator producing a 'Behavioral Specification Graph' of business rules, code transformer, equivalence validator with up to 3 feedback rounds) for COBOL/PL-SQL → Python/FastAPI modernization. On eight synthetic 195–310-line scenarios authored by one annotator, it reaches ~23% mean behavioral equivalence with GPT-4o-mini, beating single-prompt baselines only for that weak model; with GPT-4o and GPT-5.3-codex a single prompt wins.

claims.claim: With GPT-4o-mini, AgentModernize reaches 23.0% mean BER vs 12.4% SP-LLM and 4.5% CoT-LLM.
claims.evidence: Table III (3 trials, means): AM 23.0, AM-NoFB 23.9 (abstract says 23.8), SP 12.4, CoT 4.5. Most cells are 0.0; per-scenario winners vary; σ up to 48.1. Abstract says AM non-zero on 5/8 (consistent with Table III) but Table VIII lists 4/8 for the same configuration — internal inconsistency.

claims.claim: The pipeline's benefit is inversely correlated with model capability.
claims.evidence: Table VIII / §V-H: AM 15.3 vs SP 19.6 (GPT-4o), AM 7.8 vs SP 16.0 (GPT-5.3-codex). An honest negative result, but on 8 scenarios with high variance.

claims.claim: The BSG captures 92.3% of gold-standard rules at 90.2% precision; code generation is the bottleneck.
claims.evidence: Table VII; matching done manually by the same annotator who wrote the gold rules (with GPT-4o assisting rule drafting); S1 precision only 48%.

claims.claim: The feedback loop is decisive for some scenarios but regresses others.
claims.evidence: Table III: feedback raises S4/S6/S7 from 0 to 25.0/53.3/43.6 but drops S2 75.8→12.1 and S8 28.9→0.0; averages equal (23.0 vs 23.9).

claims.claim: Traceable artifacts (rule inventory, BSG, equivalence reports) provide an audit trail regulated industries need.

patterns.note: Explicit intermediate behavioral spec (BSG) extracted before codegen: high extraction recall, but end-to-end equivalence only helps weak models; single prompt wins for GPT-4o/codex.
Test-feedback repair fixes localized errors (S4/S6/S7) but causes cascading regressions (S2 −63.7 pp, S8 −28.9 pp); authors recommend keeping best iteration.
4-role pipeline beats single prompt only for GPT-4o-mini.
Business-rule inventory with explicit/implicit labels as acceptance basis.
Rule inventory and equivalence reports proposed as audit trail; unevaluated.

methodology.sample: 8 synthetic scenarios (195–310 LOC, 12–15 rules each; 7 telecom, 1 banking held-out), 3 trials.
methodology.baselines: Single-prompt and CoT single-prompt GPT-4o-mini; no LLM+feedback-without-BSG baseline (acknowledged), no agentic coding tools, no commercial modernization tools.
methodology.models: GPT-4o-mini default; GPT-4o and GPT-5.3-codex comparison.
methodology.variance: Per-cell σ listed; 20 of 32 cells σ=0; max σ=48.1; no significance tests (authors note low power).
methodology.contamination_controls: Synthetic scenarios (no public leakage), but single author designed scenarios and gold rules; S8 written after pipeline freeze.
methodology.languages: Source COBOL/PL-SQL; target Python (FastAPI), pytest — not Java.

standards.artifacts: Stated available but URL anonymized for double-blind review.

biases.detail: 195–310-line synthetic scenarios; authors note real systems are orders of magnitude larger.
Same annotator authored scenarios, gold rules, and manually matched BSG rules to gold.
Evaluation tests are generated per method by GPT-4o-mini from each method's own code/API surface, so the oracle differs across methods and depends on the same model family under test.
Baselines are single prompts with GPT-4o-mini; no single-agent + test-feedback baseline or agentic coding tool.

coi.affiliations: University of Texas at Arlington (both authors).

verdict_reason: Candid paper whose most useful findings are negative (structured multi-agent pipeline loses to a single prompt on stronger models; feedback loops regress). Evidence base is too small and self-constructed for positive claims: 8 toy synthetic scenarios, single annotator, per-method LLM-generated oracle tests, minor numeric inconsistencies (23.8 vs 23.9; 5/8 vs 4/8).
applicability: For a Java team adopting spec-driven development, this is a cautionary data point: extracting an explicit rule spec (BSG-like) before codegen gave high rule recall but did not by itself yield correct code, and with frontier models the multi-agent spec pipeline underperformed a single prompt. Keep the spec as the human-reviewable contract and audit trail (useful for healthcare-education content rules), but don't expect a role pipeline to raise correctness; invest in deterministic tests and best-iteration retention to stop feedback-loop regressions. Target language is Python, scenarios are single-file, and nothing addresses ≥4-repo coordination or agent hosts.

conflicts_with.detail: TDDev finds test-feedback loops add 15–24 pp for the strongest backbone (Sonnet 4.6) and only fail for weak testers; AgentModernize finds feedback gains shrink or reverse as models get stronger (GPT-4o, GPT-5.3-codex). Differences in oracle reliability and task size likely explain it.
